Atharva Veda Commentary [Hymn 58, Verse 5]

And for the sake of self-protection. May this cup of yours, which is the instrument of nourishment, may this battle not fail, may it not depart. The seer who has witnessed the mantra says, "Make it firm."

The eye of the sacrifice, its beginning and its face; with speech, with hearing, with mind, I offer. May the gods, being of good mind, come to this sacrifice which has been extended by <term>Vishvakarman</term> <gloss>the All-Maker</gloss>. (5)

Yajñasya. Cakṣuḥ. Prabhṛtiḥ. Mukham. Ca. Vācā. Śrotreṇa. Manasā. Juhomi.
Imam. Yajñam. Vitatam. Viśvakarmaṇā. Ā. Devāḥ. Yantu. Sumanasyamānāḥ. (5)

This stanza has been explained previously (Atharva Veda 2.35.5). I offer the senses, beginning with the eye, as being related to the sacrifice, and I make them inclined toward it. May the gods, being of good mind—acting as if they were of one mind—come to and reach this mental sacrifice, which has been spread out by the god <term>Vishvakarman</term> <gloss>the Creator of the Universe</gloss>. This is the meaning of the compilation.

Those who are the priests of the gods, and those who are worthy of sacrifice, to whom the offering is made, the portion due. May all the gods, great and powerful, come together with their wives to this sacrifice and take pleasure in it. (6)

Ye. Devānām. Ṛtvijaḥ. Ye. Ca. Yajñiyāḥ. Yebhyaḥ. Havyam. Kriyate. Bhāgadheyam.
Imam. Yajñam. Saha. Patnībhiḥ. Āitya. Yāvantaḥ. Devāḥ. Taviṣāḥ. Mādayantām. (6)

Among the gods, those who are the priests are the ones who perform the sacrifice at the proper time, becoming the <term>rtvij</term> <gloss>sacrificial priests</gloss>. Those who are worthy of sacrifice are those deserving of worship. To both of these groups of gods, the portion of the offering is given. As many as there are gods, may all those great and powerful gods, together with their respective wives—such as <term>Indrani</term> <gloss>the wife of Indra</gloss> and others—come to this sacrifice and take pleasure in it, becoming satisfied by the acceptance of the oblation.

Thus ends the fourth hymn of the seventh <term>anuvaka</term> <gloss>sub-section</gloss>.

The hymn beginning "You, Agni, are the protector of vows" is prescribed for the <term>ajya-homa</term> <gloss>offering of clarified butter</gloss> when there is a lapse in the new or full moon sacrifice, or for the setting of the sacrificial fuel for the purpose of peace. It has been codified by <term>Kausika</term> <gloss>the author of the Kausika Sutra</gloss> in the <term>Samhitavidhi</term> <gloss>ritual manual for the संहिता (collection of mantras)</gloss>.

<note>Footnote 1: Kriyate (is made) is found in manuscripts A, Bb, C, R, Sm; Kriyate in Cs; Kṛṇute (makes) in D. Footnote 2: Patnībhir-aitya (having come with wives) is found in A, K, Km, V, Dc; various readings of the same appear in Bb, Sm, R, C, D, Cs. Footnote 3: Taviṣā mād- (powerful, let them delight) is found in A, R, Cs; variants in Bb, C, D, Sm, V, K, Km, Dc; other readings noted in various manuscripts.</note>

<summary>This page provides a Sanskrit commentary on verses 5 and 6 of the 58th hymn of the seventh section of the Atharva Veda, focusing on the ritual offering and the invocation of the gods and their consorts. It concludes by noting the liturgical application of the hymn within the Kausika Sutra tradition.</summary>
